name: António Guterres
role: UN Secretary-General — Global Peace Architecture Steward
quote: There is no military solution to political conflicts. Only negotiations and compromise can produce lasting peace.

name: Moussa Faki Mahamat
role: African Union Commission Chairperson — Africa Peace & Security Architecture
quote: Silencing the guns by 2030 requires not just political will but the structural transformation of African governance and resource distribution.

name: Geir Pedersen
role: UN Special Envoy for Syria — Constitutional Committee Facilitator
quote: A genuine political process, not cosmetic change, is what Syrians need and what the international community must demand.

name: Hans Grundberg
role: UN Special Envoy for Yemen — Ceasefire and Political Process Mediator. AUG 13: Briefed UN Security Council that Yemen faces its greatest risk of renewed large-scale conflict since the April 2022 truce, citing Aug 6-7 Houthi-government clashes and renewed threats to Red Sea/Gulf of Aden shipping; proposed frontline de-escalation, an end to shipping attacks, and a halt to cross-border strikes as the path back to a political process. His warning that 'four years of calm can be lost in a few weeks of escalation' continued to frame Security Council discussion through mid-August.
quote: A negotiated settlement is within reach, but it requires all parties to prioritize the Yemeni people over military and political calculations.

name: Staffan de Mistura
role: UN Personal Envoy for Western Sahara — Roundtable Facilitator
quote: I am looking for a political solution that will be acceptable to all parties, and I am convinced that one exists.

name: Olusegun Obasanjo
role: Former AU High Representative — Ethiopia–Tigray Pretoria Mediator
quote: The Pretoria Agreement proves that Africa can solve African problems — but implementation requires the same determination as negotiation.

name: Gustavo Petro
role: Former President of Colombia — 'Total Peace' Architect; TERM ENDED AUG 7, 2026 with inauguration of De la Espriella, who is actively winding down Total Peace; Total Peace had been suspended after the Jan 2025 Catatumbo collapse — ELN and EMC/Mordisco broke off talks. As of Aug 19, former combatants who negotiated benefits under Petro's framework remain in demobilization zones (ZUTs) awaiting word on whether the new government will honor those commitments.
quote: Total Peace is the only path: we cannot continue with selective peace that leaves some armed groups to fill the vacuum. We must transform the conditions of inequality that fuel all violence.

name: Abelardo de la Espriella
role: President of Colombia (inaugurated Aug 7, 2026) — Winding down 'Total Peace'; launched a 90-day 'shock plan' offensive against armed groups (aerial bombardment, forced coca eradication) and pledged to revoke benefits granted in prior negotiations and reactivate arrest warrants. AUG 27: formalized the policy's end by ordering the extradition to the US of five individuals recognized as Total Peace negotiators (FARC dissident, ELN dissident and Los Pachenca/ACSN figures) whose 2025-approved extraditions had been suspended during the talks, declaring 'In my government, there will be no peace processes.'
quote: Total Peace was fake peace — it left the state's monopoly on force in the hands of criminal groups. We will confront them directly.

name: Iván Mordisco (Néstor Gregorio Vera)
role: Commander, FARC-EP Estado Mayor Central — Colombia Re-armed Dissident, Broke off Talks 2025
quote: We re-armed because the state never fulfilled the peace accord. The land reform, the crop substitution, the protection of former combatants — none of it was delivered.

name: Abdel Fattah al-Burhan
role: Commander, Sudan Armed Forces (SAF) — Head of Sovereignty Council. AUG 15: Pledged temporary immunity and legal/security guarantees for participants in a proposed national dialogue (not state-organized), while firmly ruling out any political comeback for RSF's Hemeti; met the AU Peace and Security Council delegation in Khartoum Aug 16.
quote: We will not negotiate under fire. The RSF must lay down arms and face justice before any political dialogue can proceed.

name: Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo 'Hemeti'
role: Commander, Rapid Support Forces (RSF) — Sudan Armed Group Leader
quote: We are fighting for a new Sudan — civilian, federal, and democratic — against a military regime that has ruled through violence for decades.

name: Abiy Ahmed Ali
role: Prime Minister of Ethiopia — Nobel Laureate, Pretoria Agreement Signatory
quote: The Pretoria Agreement opens a new chapter. Ethiopia's diversity is its strength, not its weakness, and federalism must protect every community.

name: Debretsion Gebremichael
role: Chairman, Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) — Pretoria Signatory
quote: Peace is our first demand. We signed the Pretoria Agreement because our people have suffered enough. Implementation must now deliver on every provision.

name: Salva Kiir Mayardit
role: President of South Sudan — R-ARCSS Signatory
quote: South Sudan was born in hope. The revitalized agreement gives us another chance — but our people need security, not just signatures on paper.

name: Riek Machar
role: First Vice President of South Sudan — Opposition Leader, R-ARCSS Partner
quote: The peace process is real but fragile. We cannot allow another outbreak of violence — the suffering of South Sudanese people demands we make this work.

name: Jan Egeland
role: Secretary-General, Norwegian Refugee Council — Humanitarian Diplomacy Advocate
quote: Humanitarians are not a substitute for political solutions. Every day of stalemate in Sudan, Yemen, or DRC costs lives that political leaders should be compelled to save.

name: Bankole Adeoye
role: AU Commissioner for Political Affairs, Peace and Security
quote: The African Peace and Security Architecture is maturing. We must move from reactive crisis management to proactive structural prevention of conflict.

name: Ismail Haniyeh (1963–2024)
role: Former Hamas Political Bureau Chief — Gaza Ceasefire Negotiator (assassinated July 31, 2024)
quote: We are for a ceasefire that ends the aggression and opens the crossings. But we will not accept a ceasefire that does not end the war permanently.

name: Uhuru Kenyatta
role: AU High Representative — Ethiopia–Tigray & DRC–EAC Mediator
quote: Peace cannot be imposed from outside — it must be owned by those who live it. Our role as mediators is to create space for parties to find their own solutions.

name: Ahmed al-Sharaa (Abu Mohammad al-Jolani)
role: De facto Syrian leader — Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham, Post-Assad Transitional Authority
quote: Syria needs a government that represents all Syrians — we will build institutions that protect every minority and every region, based on justice not sect.

name: Recep Tayyip Erdoğan
role: President of Turkey — Key Mediator in Ukraine–Russia & Libya
quote: Turkey is the only NATO member maintaining dialogue with both Moscow and Kyiv. We will continue this role until a just and lasting peace is achieved.

name: Massad Boulos
role: Senior Adviser to President Trump — US Sudan & Africa Peace Envoy
quote: A three-month humanitarian truce without preconditions is the only realistic first step. Both parties must choose their people over their military calculations.

name: Nikolay Mladenov
role: Chair, Board of Peace / Former UN Peace Envoy for Gaza — AUG 9: Netanyahu formally rejected the Board of Peace's 15-point Gaza roadmap, insisting on full Hamas disarmament before any IDF withdrawal; Mladenov said any Israeli pullback would instead come incrementally from areas declared weapons-free, with international forces taking over vacated ground, as Hamas reaffirmed conditional commitment to the roadmap. MAY 22: Board of Peace UNSC petition heard in the May 22 open debate — Alakbarov briefed 856 Palestinians killed since Oct ceasefire; Hamas counter-offer conditions disarmament on Palestinian statehood framework; National Transitional Committee (Ali Shaath) established as Board-supervised Gaza governance track. AUG 26: told the UN Security Council a collapsed ceasefire would be an irreversible 'point of no return' — 'no road map to return to, no administration to deploy, nothing left on the ground to rebuild' — while also criticizing Israel's continued strikes and warning the alternative to the Board's plan is 'the next war.'
quote: That would not be a setback. It would be a point of no return for everyone.

name: Steve Witkoff
role: Special Envoy, Trump Administration — Multi-track Diplomacy Lead. IRAN: Deal STILL UNSIGNED Week 16; JUN 6 mutual strikes (US downs 6 Iranian drones, Iran fires 7 missiles); Gen. Munir in Tehran Jun 6-7 seeking breakthrough; Iran demands $24B in frozen assets. Lebanon-Israel: Beirut suburbs struck Jun 7 despite US request to refrain; ceasefire near collapse; Brussels Signal: 'deal facing collapse'; Round 5 still Jun 22. Ukraine: Peskov dismisses Zelensky letter Jun 7 ('come to Moscow'); diplomatic track frozen. Colombia: runoff Jun 21.
quote: We are making progress on multiple fronts simultaneously. The President is committed to ending conflicts through strength and smart negotiation.

name: Narendra Modi
role: Prime Minister of India — Operation Sindoor Architect; India-Pakistan ceasefire (May 2025) 1-year anniversary May 10, 2026
quote: Operation Sindoor was a defining moment in India's strategic journey — our armed forces demonstrated unmatched courage, precision, and determination in dismantling the infrastructure of terrorism.

name: JD Vance
role: Vice President of the United States — Iran Talks: Deal UNSIGNED Week 16; JUN 6 mutual strikes (US downs 6 Iranian drones, Iran fires 7 missiles at Gulf); Gen. Munir in Tehran Jun 6-7 seeking breakthrough; Iran introduces $24B frozen asset demand as new precondition. Lebanon-Israel: Beirut strikes Jun 7 defy US request; ceasefire near collapse; Brussels Signal: 'facing collapse.' Congressional opposition (52 senators, 177 House members) continues to constrain signing. Vance Jun 3: 'hard to say exactly when or if the president's going to sign.'
quote: The President has made clear: we will achieve a deal through strength, or we will achieve our objectives another way. Iran knows what is required.

name: Marco Rubio
role: U.S. Secretary of State — Lebanon–Israel: JUN 7 Israel strikes Beirut suburbs despite Rubio's explicit request to refrain; ceasefire near collapse; Round 5 still Jun 22 as last realistic opportunity before Jun 29 deadline. Ukraine: Rubio says US 'stands ready' after Peskov dismisses Zelensky letter Jun 7 — no imminent breakthrough; diplomatic track frozen entering summer. Iran: deal unsigned Week 16; mutual strikes Jun 6; Rubio working Munir/Pakistan channel alongside Witkoff.
quote: We are pursuing durable security arrangements for Lebanon that require full implementation of UNSC Resolution 1701 — Israeli withdrawal and Lebanese sovereignty must go hand in hand.

name: Nawaf Salam
role: Prime Minister of Lebanon — Ceasefire Extension Negotiator, Washington Talks Apr 22–23 2026
quote: Lebanon's sovereignty is non-negotiable. A durable ceasefire requires the complete withdrawal of Israeli forces from Lebanese territory and the full implementation of Resolution 1701.

name: Joseph Aoun
role: President of Lebanon — Sovereignty Architect, Oversees Lebanon–Israel Direct Talks Apr–May 2026
quote: This is an opportunity that may not arise again. Lebanon must emerge from these talks as a fully sovereign state — with Israeli forces withdrawn, detainees returned, and our reconstruction begun. We will not accept a ceasefire that is merely a pause in our subordination.

name: Naim Qassem
role: Secretary-General of Hezbollah — Succeeded Nasrallah (Sep 2024); May 12: Urged Lebanon to quit Washington talks. JUN 4: PUBLICLY REJECTED Round 4 conditional ceasefire framework, calling it 'absurd, humiliating, and shameful' — said the deal amounts to a demand for surrender while Israeli military operations continue. Hezbollah continued rocket and drone attacks on northern Israel Jun 4-5; renewed strikes on Israeli positions in south Lebanon. Position: unconditional Israeli withdrawal must be Phase 1 precondition; Hezbollah will not accept LAF-only zone framework that excludes resistance from its own territory.
quote: We will not accept a peace process that legitimizes the enemy's occupation or bypasses Lebanon's resistance. Any agreement that demands our disarmament while Israel continues its aggression is not a ceasefire — it is surrender.

name: General Asim Munir
role: Chief of Army Staff, Pakistan — Key US-Iran Mediator. MAY 31: Deal STILL UNSIGNED Day 3+ post-tentative agreement; Trump ended May 29 meeting without final determination (CNBC); IRGC Gen. Rezaei warned May 30 of blockade attack if Trump betrays deal; Hormuz blocked Week 14. Munir continues as principal intermediary connecting US team (Vance, Witkoff, Kushner) with Iranian side (Qalifbaf/Khamenei's office). Pakistan hosted both Islamabad rounds (Apr 11-12, Apr 26) and transmitted Iran's MOU response (May 10).
quote: Pakistan stands ready to facilitate dialogue. We have always believed that dialogue is the only sustainable path to peace in the region.

name: Recep Tayyip Erdoğan
role: President of Turkey — Istanbul hosted BOTH Ukraine-Russia direct talks (May 15–16, collapsed; Putin absent) AND Iran-EU3 nuclear talks (first since April ceasefire) — reinforcing Ankara's role as global peace hub; May 19: Russia FM signals readiness to return to Istanbul format for future Ukraine-Russia rounds
quote: Turkey is the only NATO member maintaining dialogue with both Moscow and Kyiv. We will continue this role until a just and lasting peace is achieved.

name: Mazloum Abdi
role: Commander, Syrian Democratic Forces — AUG 20: Announced completion of Kurdish-led military, security, and administrative integration into Syrian state institutions, implementing the Jan 29, 2026 Damascus-SDF agreement. Said 'the next battle will be political' — Kurdish constitutional rights remain unresolved and Damascus has not yet integrated all-women SDF units.
quote: The military and security integration phase is complete and finished. The next battle will be political.

name: Sergey Ryabkov
role: Deputy Foreign Minister of Russia — AUG 21: Said Moscow is open to 'new ideas' on ending the Ukraine war, but only if they match Putin's preconditions (Donbas cession, demilitarization, no NATO membership) and reflect 'current military realities.' Credited the Trump administration with showing 'an understanding of Russia's position.'
quote: We are open to new ideas, but they must correspond to the goals set by the president and reflect the realities on the ground.
